$comment: Generated by schemars from the Rust types the socket carries: change those and run `cargo test -p p02-gateway contract`.

AccessLevel.description: How much of a service: ordered, so `Write` satisfies a need for `Read`.

oneOf.description: Nothing was written.
Her package could not be written, and is as it was.

AddCharacterOutcome.description:
What came of adding the character a file holds. `added`: she is new
here; `updated`: her package replaced the one installed. Either way her
package is on disk, and she starts as any enabled character does.

oneOf.description: The file holds no character this home can publish.
She comes with the app.

Answer.description: The person's answer to a parked confirmation or a pairing request.

AnswerBody.description: The person's answer, to a confirmation or a pairing request alike.

AnswerOutcome.description:
What an answer to a parked confirmation came to. `expired`: the deadline
had passed, so the confirmation was settled cancelled instead; the
client is never the judge of the deadline.

Authored.description: What the target's own document holds for a field.

oneOf.description: It is receiving messages.
Its service refused its token.
Its service cannot be reached.
Another program is polling its token.
Its token is set to a webhook.

BotState.description: How a bot stands. A bot that does not know yet is in no table.

BotUsername.description:
The name a bot goes by on its connector's service, without the `@`: 1
to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores, as Telegram spells one.

oneOf.description: The documents changed after its author read them.
The change, or the settings it would leave, is not one to make.
No installed character answers to its target.

CharacterConnectorEntry.description:
A connector's section for one target: its activation, and each field
that has a value it takes for that target, the home's fields reaching
every character's entry.

oneOf.description: A plugin of this build, by the name a page shows.
A plugin her file asks for that this build does not have.

CharacterFeature.description: A feature a character would start with.

oneOf.description: She is new here.
This very version of her is installed.
Another version of her is installed: adding her updates her.
She comes with the app: she cannot be added.

CharacterInstalled.description: Whether the character a file holds is in the home already.

about.description: One line about her, when her file has one.

comesWith.description:
The features she would start with: each plugin on by default or
asked for by her file, in the plugin list's order, then each one
her file asks for that this build does not have.

hasData.description:
Whether a data folder of hers is in the home: she was here
before, and her chats come back with her.

CharacterPreviewOutcome.description:
Who a character file holds and what adding her would do, judged as an
add judges it, or why she cannot be added from it.

oneOf.description: The file holds no character this home can publish.

Her settings give her no AI model she can use: she is built
without one, and the lines sent to her wait until they do.

builtIn.description:
Whether she comes with the app: she can be switched off, never
removed.

diagnostic.description:
Why she failed, what she needs for a model, or what her start
warned of.

maintenance.description: The latest background failure since she started.

CharacterSummary.description: One installed character, as health reports her.

ClientStamp.description:
What a client stamps on a line it carries: the surface it came from, or
the id it submitted the line under, which a repeat of the line reuses. An
ASCII letter or digit, then up to 63 ASCII letters, digits, `:`, `.`, `_`
or `-`.

oneOf.description: A document that cannot be read, is not JSON, or is no object.

A key the settings do not know, or a namespace that is no
object: not used.

A value its field does not take: not used, and nothing stands in
for it.
A value her package gives that a package may not set.

A plugin she does not run that her package expects, or that she
has switched on before its setup is finished.

Code.description: What a finding is, in the one spelling clients read.

ConfigChange.description: One change to one document, bound to the fingerprint its author read.

ConfigChangeOutcome.description:
What came of a change. `Applied` means the document is on disk, under
the fingerprint it now has; `Refused` is the change itself, and
`Failed` a write that could not be made, either leaving every document
as it was.

ConfigTarget.description:
Whose settings a view reads or a change writes, and whose bot a
connector's is: the home's, or one character's.

oneOf.description: A place on the person's machine.
A server the plugin sends to.

ConfigValueType.description:
The kind of value a config field holds. Whether it holds a
credential is the field's `secret` flag alone to say.

ConfigView.description:
What a settings screen renders: the fingerprint a change must present,
the diagnostics, whether the target's settings give a character an AI
model, and the host's fields and every section the target may set, all
in one field shape. A target whose settings cannot be resolved is
refused with the reason, never shown as blank fields.

oneOf.description: Nobody answered by the deadline.
Her character stopped.

ConfirmationId.description:
A parked confirmation's id: a fresh UUID, unique across the daemon, by
which any surface answers it.

ConfirmationQuestion.description:
What the person is asked about: the plugin and tool whose call it is,
what the tool says it does, and what the call would do.

ConfirmationSettlement.description:
How a confirmation ended: with the person's answer, or cancelled and
why.

ConnectorBot.description:
One bot a connector runs, as the connector says it stands: whose it is,
the home's own or one character's, the name it goes by once its service
has said who it is, and its state. Its token is no part of it.

ConnectorBotsBody.description:
A connector's bot table, whole every time: the daemon holds it in place
of the one it held, never beside it.

ConnectorBotsOutcome.description:
What came of a connector's bot table. `kept`: health shows it from now
on, until the connector's last stream ends.

oneOf.description:
No stream of the connector is open, and a table is kept only while
one is.

ConnectorConfigEntry.description:
A connector's section for one target: its activation, and each field
that has a value it takes for that target, the home's fields reaching
every character's entry.

ConnectorConfigView.description:
What a connector runs on: an entry for the home and one for each
installed character that is switched on, in roster order, each with
its section's activation and, while that is active, the values in
effect for it, secrets in the clear. The home's switch is a default,
not a master switch: each entry is judged by its own.

ConnectorPresence.description:
Whether a process of a built-in connector is on the event stream now,
and the bots it last said it runs, none while it is not.

ConversationId.description:
A conversation: an ASCII letter or digit, then up to 55 ASCII letters,
digits, `_` or `-`. It holds no `.`, which is what parts it from the
segment number in the id of each of its sessions, and its length leaves
that id room for the segment within the 64 characters a tool admits.

EffectiveView.description:
The value in effect: authored in a document, `config`; the declared
default, `default`; or none, `missing`. A refused value is in effect
unresolved, its value shown unless it is a secret's.

Fingerprint.description:
A value's identity, comparable without the value: `sha256:` and the
lowercase hex SHA-256 of its [`canonical_json`].

GatewayErrorBody.description:
The one shape every transport refusal takes; a verb's outcome never
uses it.

oneOf.description:
A turn's progress: each message once it is durable, and the tool
calls of its rounds.

A turn as it runs now, said whenever that changes, from the commit
of her line until the completion that ends it.

How a turn ended, with its line's stamps, so that a surface knows
whose turn ended and whether its line is in the log.

How a confirmation ended: with the person's answer, or cancelled and
why.

message.description:
Present when a failure caused the change, or when she needs a
model: what to do about it.

oneOf.description:
The daemon's whole state read again: when the settings changed,
before the pass that acts on them, and when a connector came onto
the stream or left it.

A background failure the conversation never sees: the plugins' work
after a turn's commit, a segment rotation that failed, which the next
turn plans again, what closing a segment left undone, or what opening
her thread skipped because it could not be read.

config.description: What the home's settings document says of itself.

packages.description: The packages discovery could not publish, which the roster lacks.

GatewayHealth.description: The daemon's whole state in one read.

GatewayMessage.description:
The person's line into one conversation, with the two stamps its client
puts on it: which surface carried it, and the id a repeat of the same
submission reuses.

GatewayReady.description:
The first frame of a stream that cannot be caught up: the state every
later frame moves on from.

GatewayRefusalReason.description: Why a line was refused before any turn ran.

HistoryMessage.description:
A committed message as the scrollback shows it, with the stamps its
client put on the person's line and when it was committed.

Identifier.description:
A Project02 identifier: an ASCII letter, then up to 127 ASCII letters,
digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. Characters, plugins and tools are named by one.

advanced.description:
Whether the card holds what most people leave as it is: a page may
keep a row of it out of sight while nothing sets its field.

when.description: When the card's rows have an effect.

LayoutCard.description:
One card of a section's layout: rows of its fields, under a title and
over a footer when it has them.

when.description: When the field has an effect, beyond its card's own condition.

LayoutRow.description: One row of a card: a field of the section.

LayoutWhen.description:
A condition on a field of the same section that lists its allowed
values: it holds while that field's value in effect is one of `is`.
What it guards has no effect otherwise, so a page may hide it then.

MaintenanceFailure.description:
A background failure the conversation never sees: the plugins' work
after a turn's commit, a segment rotation that failed, which the next
turn plans again, what closing a segment left undone, or what opening
her thread skipped because it could not be read.

OpenConversationBody.description: The character whose thread with the person to open.

OpenOutcome.description: What came of opening a character's thread with the person.

Operation.description:
What a change does: sets or unsets a host field, by its path
`project02.<name>`; switches a section on or off, or leaves it to the
document beneath when `enabled` is absent; or sets or unsets one field
of a section.

PackageReport.description: A package discovery could not publish, and why, where.

PairingDecision.description:
How a pairing request ended: with the person's answer, or at its
deadline.

code.description: Six digits, unique among the requests waiting.

source.description:
The connector's endpoint the account first wrote to, as the stamp
its lines will carry: for Telegram, `telegram:<bot username>`.

expiresAt.description: When the request expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

PairingRequest.description:
An account a connector asks to let in, waiting for the person's answer
under a code any surface shows and answers by, until it expires.

source.description:
The connector's endpoint the account wrote to, as the stamp its
lines will carry: for Telegram, `telegram:<bot username>`.

PairingRequestBody.description: The account a connector asks the person to let in, and where it wrote.

PairingRequestOutcome.description:
What came of a connector's request to let an account in. `paired`: the
home lets it in already, so nothing is asked.

PairingSettleOutcome.description:
What an answer to a pairing request came to. `expired`: the deadline had
passed, so the request was settled expired instead, as a confirmation
is; `failed`: the approval could not be written, and the request waits
on.

PairingSubject.description:
The account a pairing is for: the connector's own id for it, and the
name the person sees.

PairingSubjectBody.description:
The account a pairing is for: its id a stamp, and its name within the
bound of a name a person goes by, which the daemon judges further.

deadlineAt.description: When the confirmation expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

turn.description: The turn that raised it; none for a call raised outside any turn.

PendingConfirmation.description: A parked confirmation, as the stream announced it and the list shows it.

oneOf.description: Among what makes up her mind and body.
Among what she is permitted to do.

Placement.description: Where a plugin's row belongs on a settings page.

icon.description:
A name of the page's own set, as `tint` is: a page falls back for
one it does not know.

order.description:
Where the row comes among its placement's: by this, then by
display name.

connection.description:
What the plugin's entry among a page's connections is called, for
a plugin whose home settings are an account set up once.

PluginPage.description:
How a plugin's row on a settings page is drawn, as its manifest
declares it.

Refusal.description: A transport refusal: the envelope's code and sentence.

oneOf.description: Nothing was removed.
Her package could not be removed, and is as it was.

RemoveCharacterOutcome.description:
What came of removing a character. `removed`: her package is gone and
she stops; her data stays, for her to come back to.

oneOf.description: She comes with the app: she can be switched off, never removed.
No package of the home holds her.

RosterState.description:
Where an installed character stands as health reports her: her
runtime's state, or `not_started` until the daemon built it.

RunningDraft.description: A reply she is still writing: its text so far, under its draft's id.

RunningTurn.description:
A turn as it runs: the line that started it, her character, and her
drafts so far, each its whole text, in the order they opened.

RuntimeConfigDiagnostic.description:
A finding about the settings: its weight, its code, a sentence for a
person that never repeats a value, the place in the document, what it
concerns, the settings as a whole or one section, and, for a finding in
a character's overlay, whose.

label.description: What a page calls the field.

choices.description:
The words for each allowed value, which a page lists in the order
of `allowedValues`.

RuntimeConfigFieldInspectShape.description:
One field as a screen shows it: its declaration, what the target's own
document holds for it, and the value in effect with where it comes
from, a secret's as `[redacted]`.

RuntimeConfigSectionActivationShape.description: Whether a section runs, as its settings decide it, and why.

page.description: How a plugin's row is drawn, when its manifest says.

access.description:
What a plugin's manifest requests, each access with its level; a
connector has none.

enabledSource.description: Which document decides `enabled`, or the declaration's default.

setup.description:
Whether its settings are enough to build it, judged switched on or
off: a plugin switched on before they are does not run. A
connector's always are.

layout.description: The cards `fields` are drawn in, each field in one at least.

RuntimeConfigSectionInspectShape.description: One section as a screen shows it.

RuntimeConfigSectionNamespace.description:
The two stanzas of a document that hold declared sections by id. A
plugin and a connector may share an id: their sections never meet.

Setup.description:
Whether settings are enough for what they set up, a plugin or a
character's AI model; while they are not, `message` says what to fill
in, in the words of the settings page.

Severity.description:
How much a finding weighs: an error stops what it concerns, a warning
only says so.

Short.description:
A string of 1 to 128 characters, as an id is on the wire, and the name
an account goes by.

Source.description:
Where a value in effect comes from: its field's declared default, the
home's settings, or the character's own.

SpeakerName.description:
The name a speaker goes by on a message: one line of at most 128
characters, without blank space at either end. It is set before a
colon in chat, which is why a line break is refused.

StartOutcome.description:
What an explicit start came to: `settled` says it ran, and the summary's
state says how it ended.

StorageFailure.description:
An ordinary failure of the home's storage, a full disk, a permission or
a damaged record, which the person is told and which is no bug.

oneOf.description: In her inbox now, behind every line before it.
In her inbox already, under the same id.
Refused before it was queued.
Her inbox could not take it.

SubmitOutcome.description:
What became of a line sent to a character: queued in her inbox, where
she takes it in its turn and the stream tells how that ended, or
refused at once.

Text.description: A line's text, as long as a line may be.

Timestamp.description:
A moment, in the one spelling every record uses: UTC to the
millisecond, `2026-06-15T00:00:00.000Z`. Text order is time order.

ToolCallStatus.description: How a call of a round came back: as its plugin answered, or refused.

TurnIdentity.description: The submission a turn runs for, which any surface can tell as its own.

TurnProgress.description: What a turn says as it goes, in order.

TurnStatus.description: How a turn ended, as the frame announcing it says.

VisibleMessageRole.description:
Which side of a conversation someone speaks for: a character, or the
person. A visible message carries its speaker's, and the two order as
they are spelled, characters first.

VisibleText.description:
Text as a person sees it: line endings are `\n`, neither end is blank
space, and something is left.
